tested_scope: Exactly one deterministic self-local replay continuing the prior generation-scoped idempotency-key result. One intended logical effect generation G1 has durable identity K1=(logical_effect,G1). The replay tests crash/interruption before first durable accept, acknowledgement loss after atomic accept, repeated cross-invocation interruption/rate-limit boundaries, claimant turnover while G1 remains pending, and a non-atomic negative control where an external effect can occur before durable K1 binding. It tests only abstract claim/idempotency behavior and cross-run continuation; no concrete transport, public source, O/downstream/other-worker state, shared ledger, scheduler mutation, hosted compute, richer-mode arbitration, finite quota, or optional second semantic leaf is modeled.

retained_assumptions: K1 is stable for exactly one intended logical effect generation G1 and is preserved across retries and claimant turnover until G1 reaches a terminal accepted result.
A current-authority or fencing predicate is checked immediately before each attempt; stale claimants cannot initiate a new accepted attempt after turnover.

For the positive controls, apply_once(K1,P1) atomically couples durable idempotency-key binding with the effect outcome: either no accepted effect exists, or K1 is durably bound to the one accepted result before a retry can create another accepted effect.
Cross-invocation state can durably preserve pending K1 and retry intent without relying on a finite monthly/trial/paid quota.
replay_schedule: C1 crash-before-first-accept: current claimant A0 attempts K1, but interruption occurs before atomic acceptance and no accepted effect exists. A later invocation retries the same K1; if one attempt eventually reaches atomic acceptance, exactly one accepted effect results.

C2 acknowledgement-loss-after-accept: K1 atomically accepts once but A0 loses the response before checkpointing success. A later retry of the same K1 returns the already-bound result and does not create a second accepted effect.

C3 repeated interruption/rate-limit boundaries: each invocation checkpoints pending K1 and returns without same-run waiting. Safety is preserved by same-key retry, but liveness is not established if every future attempt is interrupted or rate-limited; eventual progress requires a fairness/eventual-success assumption.

C4 claimant turnover while pending: authority moves from A0 to A1. A stale A0 resume is rejected by fencing. A1 must inherit and retry the same generation identity K1; allocating a fresh key K2 for the still-same G1 creates ambiguity and can duplicate an already accepted-but-unobserved K1 effect.

N1 non-atomic external-effect negative control: an external effect occurs, then interruption happens before durable K1 binding. A retry sees no bound K1 and performs the effect again. Generation-scoped identity plus fencing is insufficient without atomic effect/idempotency coupling or an equivalent transactional/deduplicating sink.

observations: Generation-scoped keys solve the prior ABA false-suppression problem only when the same generation identity survives retries and claimant turnover; a new claimant must not mint a fresh effect key merely because ownership changed.

Crash-before-first-accept and acknowledgement-loss are safely retryable with the same K1 only under an atomic apply-once contract (or an equivalent downstream deduplicating transaction) that prevents an effect from becoming externally real without durable K1 identity.
Fencing and idempotency remain orthogonal: fencing excludes stale claimants, while durable same-generation effect identity collapses retries by the current claimant or successor.

No-loss liveness cannot be proven from retry logic alone. If every future invocation is interrupted or rate-limited, the effect can remain pending forever; eventual progress requires an explicit fairness/eventual-success assumption and durable preservation of pending K1 across boundaries.
The non-atomic negative control falsifies any claim that generation-scoped keys plus fencing alone provide exactly-once external effects when the side effect can precede durable idempotency binding.
inference: Within this exact abstract replay, a recurring-Chat coordination design can preserve duplicate safety across crash/retry and claimant turnover only if one logical effect generation keeps one durable effect identity across all claimants, stale claimants are fenced, and accepted effect plus idempotency binding is atomic (or the sink itself deduplicates atomically). Eventual no-loss additionally requires durable pending-state reconstruction and a fairness/eventual-success condition; finite quota or same-run waiting cannot supply that guarantee under the Phase-1 constraints. This does not prove that an allowed concrete Chat-exposed primitive provides those semantics.
unresolved_children: A concrete allowed zero-cost quota-independent Chat-exposed primitive exposing atomic durable apply-once plus current-authority validation remains unverified.
A concrete zero-quota mechanism for transferring pending generation identity K1 across claimant turnover without ABA/collision remains unverified.

The required fairness/eventual-success condition for cross-invocation retries has not been mapped to a concrete scheduler/transport guarantee; persistent rate limiting or permanent unavailability remains a liveness blocker rather than a completion condition.
Exactly-once behavior for non-transactional external side effects remains unresolved when the effect can occur before durable idempotency binding.
